Proposal

Plugin configuration of routes in the recipe

proposal/plugin-configuration2026-11-15Giovanni Porcaridraft

Problem

The code of an application sets the plugin options of each route in @route(...): the auth rule, the channel channels, the openapi options, the env requirements. Every installation of that application gets the same values.

An installation cannot change them. The plugins section of the recipe switches plugins on for all the applications together and does not address a route. Changing an option at runtime would need a management application that does not exist.

Each installation must be able to decide the rules of its routes in its recipe, without a management application.

Proposed solution

Behaviour

  • The recipe of an installation names a route of an application and writes the options of one plugin for it.
  • The value of the recipe replaces the value written in @route(...) for that route. The two are not combined.
  • A route the recipe does not name keeps the value of the code.
  • The recipe can close a route the code leaves open and open a route the code closes.
  • Two installations of the same code have different rules.
  • No management application is needed: the recipe is enough.
  • A route named in the recipe that does not exist gives at most a warning. The boot goes on.
  • The plugin configuration can change on a running server, like other parts of the configuration. A subscription updates the plugins when it changes.

Recipe

The example application Shop attaches a section products with three routes. In the code list has no rule; insert and delete have auth_rule="shop_admin". Their URLs are /shop/products/list, /shop/products/insert, /shop/products/delete.

  • plugin_configuration is an element of ApplicationGrammar: every application has it, _server included. It is written only under an application element.
  • One plugin_configuration block names one plugin. The plugins are configured separately.
  • Each configure line carries route and the parameters of the configure method of that plugin. route is the path of one route, or the paths of several routes separated by commas. Each path is complete, relative to the application, written as in the URL after the mount, without a leading slash.
  • Every plugin present on the router of the application can be configured, a plugin registered from outside included.
  • _server is configured by declaring application(code="_server", app_class=ServerApplication) in the recipe and writing plugin_configuration under it.

What kajenn calls

kajenn adds no syntax of its own for the options: each configure line becomes one call of routing.configure of genro-routes on the routing class that owns the route.

  • The plugin of the block gives the first part of the target. The path gives the routing class and the name of the entry.
  • After these calls /shop/products/list asks for the tag staff and answers on the channel mcp too; /shop/products/delete asks for boss instead of shop_admin; /shop/products/insert asks for staff instead of shop_admin.
  • A KeyError of routing.configure (no entry with that name) becomes the warning.
  • A route of a section attached after the hook ran does not exist when the hook runs: its line is a line that names a route that does not exist.
  • A line that names a plugin that is not on the router, or an option the plugin does not know, is not applied either. Nothing stops.
must-not
kajenn adds no defensive code against errors in the plugin configuration: no boot stop, no restore of earlier values, no handling of a hook that refuses.
Defensive code prevents only the stupid errors; the dangerous ones pass anyway. An error has consequences for who made it.

The plugin_configuration hook

  • Every application has a hook plugin_configuration, marked @broadcast_hook (kajenn-org/kajenn#142).
  • The server calls it on every application with applications_broadcast("plugin_configuration").
  • The default does nothing. RoutedApplication reads its plugin_configuration blocks from the recipe and makes the calls above. An application with no block in the recipe does nothing.
  • A subclass redefines the hook to refuse a configuration or to take the export of its router before the configuration is applied.
  • No hook runs after the configuration is applied.
  • For an application declared with spawner the hook runs in the spawned process, where the application is built. Who calls it there at boot is open (d-spawned-boot).

Changes on a running server

  • The server calls the hook in the lifespan startup, before on_startup: no request arrives before the configuration.
  • After the boot the plugin_configuration blocks of an application can change in the configuration of the running server.
  • A change on a running server is a new configuration. There are no actions that insert or delete a single line: the new configuration only says which values there are.
  • A subscription updates the plugins of that application with the values of the new configuration.
  • To give a route its code value back, the new configuration writes that value.
  • An application declared with spawner needs nothing specific to plugins. Any change of the configuration, of plugins or of anything else, is carried to the spawned process, which applies it to its own configuration. Its own subscriptions fire there, the one of plugin_configuration included.
  • The hook runs before any configuration that does not come from the code: the subscription goes through the hook of that application, so the application can refuse a change made on a running server too.

Reading what the recipe changed

  • kajenn adds no log line, no route and no discovery field for this.
  • nodes() called with the tags of a user says which routes that user may execute. discover already does it.
  • routing.configure("?") gives the values in force.
  • Who wants the differences takes the export in the hook, before the configuration is applied, and keeps it. A method compares that export with the export taken when it is called. After the configuration is applied the router no longer holds the values of the code: the first export cannot be rebuilt later from the running server.

JSON form

A JSON form of the plugin configuration, such as the one an administration page would send, is set aside for now (owner, 2026-11-15). Its shape is not decided and it is not part of this proposal.

genro-routes#74

The options written by the recipe are not exposed to genro-org/genro-routes#74: they are written with routing.configure after the plugin is on the router, not read from the decorator. The hook must run after server.arm_router has plugged the plugins of the plugins section; before that, a block naming one of them meets a router without that plugin.

Decisions

decidedd-place
Where does the recipe hold the plugin options of the routes?
  1. Under each application element
    • The path is relative to the application.
    • Removing the application from the recipe removes its options.
    • An application added to a running server and the spawned process of an application find the options in the node they already read.
    • The changed rules of an installation sit in one place per application.
  2. One section for the whole server
    • All the changed rules are read in one place.
    • Each line names the application; a line can name an application that is not there.
  3. Both: from the server or from the application
Choice: Under each application element (GP, 2026-11-15)
Plugin configurations belong to the application only. The form starting from the server was admitted during the discussion and then withdrawn.
decidedd-element-name
What is the name of the element under application?
  1. plugin

    The server-level plugins section already has plugin children with another function: switching plugins on.

  2. plugin_configuration
Choice: plugin_configuration (GP, 2026-11-15)
decidedd-shape
How is a configuration written inside the application?
  1. From the route: route(path).configure(...)

    All the options changed on one route are read together. Each line must also name the plugin.

  2. One block per plugin: plugin_configuration('auth'), then configure(path, options)

    All the rules of one plugin are read in one block. The options changed on one route sit in one block per plugin.

  3. One block per application, each line with the target "plugin/path"

    A list of these lines is already a JSON form.

Choice: One block per plugin: plugin_configuration('auth'), then configure(path, options) (GP, 2026-11-15)
From a human point of view the plugins are configured separately.
decidedd-arguments
What does a configure line carry?
  1. What routing.configure asks: the path and the parameters of the plugin (rule, channels)
  2. The keywords of @route: auth_rule, channel_channels
Choice: What routing.configure asks: the path and the parameters of the plugin (rule, channels) (GP, 2026-11-15)
kajenn calls the configure of the routing class: what the recipe holds is what that method asks.
decidedd-plugins
Which plugins can the recipe configure?
  1. Every plugin present on the router
    • No list to maintain in kajenn; a plugin registered from outside is configured like the others.
    • The recipe can change the contract of a route: pydantic with disabled removes the validation, openapi with method changes the HTTP method the route answers.
  2. A closed list: auth, channel, env, openapi
Choice: Every plugin present on the router (GP, 2026-11-15)
decidedd-missing-route
What happens when the recipe names a route that does not exist?
  1. The boot stops
  2. At most a warning; the boot goes on
Choice: At most a warning; the boot goes on (GP, 2026-11-15)
decidedd-visibility
Where does one read which options the recipe changed?
  1. Log lines when the configuration is applied
  2. A route of _server listing the changed options
  3. A field in the discovery and in the OpenAPI document
  4. Nothing added: nodes() for a user and the export of genro-routes
Choice: Nothing added: nodes() for a user and the export of genro-routes (GP, 2026-11-15)
Calling nodes as a user says whether that user can or cannot. genro-routes has an export of the configuration.
decidedd-after-hook
Does a second hook run after the configuration is applied?
  1. Yes: the pair before and after gives the two exports to compare
  2. No: a method compares the export taken before with the current state
Choice: No: a method compares the export taken before with the current state (GP, 2026-11-15)
Who wants the differences has a method that takes the saved export and compares it with the current state.
decidedd-hook
Who applies the configuration, and who can refuse it or take the export before it is applied?
  1. A plugin_configuration hook of the application, called with applications_broadcast
    • Words of the owner, 2026-11-15: a hook before any configuration that does not come from the code, to refuse it or to take the export; a hook plugin_configuration that does nothing when there is nothing; a broadcast of plugin configuration.
    • The hook that applies the recipe and the hook that can refuse or take the export are one method, redefined by the subclass.
    • The author of an application can refuse a change on its own routes.
  2. A hook of the server, one for all the applications

    One place takes the export of every application. The author of an application cannot refuse anything.

  3. Both: the server hook, then the application hook
Choice: A plugin_configuration hook of the application, called with applications_broadcast (GP, 2026-11-15)
A hook plugin_configuration that does nothing when there is nothing: a broadcast of plugin configuration.
decidedd-section-path
How does one line give a value to several routes, for example to all the routes of the section products?
  1. A write at router level, as genro-routes does
    • kajenn calls routing.configure("auth", rule="staff") on the section.
    • list asks for staff. insert and delete keep shop_admin, because the code gives them a rule. No message says so.
  2. Every route under the section
    • kajenn calls routing.configure("auth/*", rule="staff") on the section and on every section under it.
    • A longer path wins, whatever the order of the lines.
    • A route added by a new version of the application takes the rule of the installation.
  3. A path must end with the name of an entry; the last segment accepts the glob of the method
    • 'products/*' covers the three routes; 'products/insert,delete' covers two; 'products' alone gives the warning.
    • The glob does not descend into the sections under products.
    • Two lines on the same route are decided by the order of writing.
  4. route holds several complete paths separated by commas

    Every route is written by name. No glob and no path of a section.

Choice: route holds several complete paths separated by commas (GP, 2026-11-15)
decidedd-moment
When does the server call the hook?
  1. In the lifespan startup, before on_startup
    • No request arrives before the configuration, also for _server and in the spawned process of an application, which answer at once.
    • applications_broadcast is async and register_application is sync: the call cannot sit in the registration.
    • A section attached in on_startup or later does not exist yet: its lines give the warning and are not applied.
  2. After on_startup, before ready
    • The sections attached in on_startup exist.
    • _server and the applications of a spawned process already answer while on_startup runs: in that interval the rule of the code is in force.
Choice: In the lifespan startup, before on_startup (GP, 2026-11-15)
Before. The configurations can also change on a running server, like other things: a subscription updates the plugins when the configuration changes.
decidedd-runtime-update
How does the subscription update the plugins when the configuration of a running server changes?
  1. Only the values the new configuration holds are applied
    • One routing.configure call per value in the new configuration.
    • A route the new configuration does not name keeps the value it has: the value of the code is no longer on the router.
  2. The values of the code are restored, then the whole block is applied again
    • A written, changed or removed line is handled the same way.
    • kajenn takes the export of the router before the first configuration and keeps it for the life of the application.
    • The kept export is the one d-diff-method compares with the current state.
Choice: Only the values the new configuration holds are applied (GP, 2026-11-15)
A change cannot take a line away. It can only say which values there are: there are no insert or delete actions, only the new configuration.
decidedd-runtime-spawned
How does a change of the plugin configuration reach the application of a spawned process?
  1. A message of its own: the main process sends the plugin configuration over the KajennBus
  2. It does not: the spawned process reads the new configuration when it is relaunched
  3. Nothing specific to plugins: every change of the configuration is carried to the spawned process
Choice: Nothing specific to plugins: every change of the configuration is carried to the spawned process (GP, 2026-11-15)
The problem is generic. When a process is remote, any change of the configuration, not only of plugins, must be carried to the remote process, which applies it; doing so fires its own subscriptions.
decidedd-added-application
How does an application added to a running server receive the hook?
  1. The hook is called on that application alone, before its on_startup
  2. A new broadcast, which calls the hook again on every application
Choice: The hook is called on that application alone, before its on_startup (GP, 2026-11-15)
decidedd-invalid-line
What happens when a line names a plugin that is not on the router, or an option the plugin does not know?
  1. The boot stops
  2. The line is not applied and the boot goes on, as for a route that does not exist
Choice: The line is not applied and the boot goes on, as for a route that does not exist (GP, 2026-11-15)
Nothing happens. Whoever wrote the line wrong answers for it.
decidedd-refusal
How does a hook refuse a configuration, and what does the server do then?
  1. The subclass does not call the base: nothing is applied and nothing is reported
  2. The hook raises: on_error logs it and the broadcast goes on
  3. The hook raises: the boot stops
Choice: The subclass does not call the base: nothing is applied and nothing is reported (GP, 2026-11-15)
As a rule, errors cannot be prevented with defensive code at every moment. If there are errors there are consequences. Only the stupid errors can be prevented; the dangerous ones pass anyway.
proposedd-spawned-boot
At boot, who calls the hook of an application declared with spawner? The broadcast of the main process runs before on_startup, and RemoteApplication.on_startup is what waits for the spawned process to join: a hook forwarded before that has no process to answer it. The spawned process is a server too and has its own lifespan.
  1. The spawned process, in its own lifespan startup

    Default of this outline. It is settled during the implementation on a branch.

    • The hook runs before any request of that process, like in the main process.
    • RemoteApplication defines plugin_configuration itself, so the name stays local and is not forwarded, as it does for on_startup.
  2. The main process, with the forwarded hook, once the spawned process has joined
    • No method to add to RemoteApplication.
    • The spawned process answers requests from its start: between its start and the forwarded call the values of the code are in force.
proposedd-diff-method
Who provides the method that compares the saved export with the current state, and what is its name?
  1. kajenn provides it on the application

    Candidate name from the words of the owner: config_diff. kajenn then also takes and keeps the export.

  2. Each application that wants it writes it in its own hook

    Default of this outline. It is settled during the implementation on a branch.

    asqueel-migration makes the same comparison of two dicts with the library dictdiffer, which is not a dependency of kajenn.

decidedd-keywords
Which keywords carry the plugin and the path in the recipe? A value written without a name is lost on a node that receives children, so the plugin of plugin_configuration needs a keyword.
  1. plugin_configuration(code="auth") and configure(path="products/list", ...)

    code is the keyword of the existing plugin element.

  2. plugin_configuration(plugin="auth") and configure(target="products/list", ...)

    target is the word of routing.configure.

  3. plugin_configuration(plugin="auth") and configure(route="products/list", ...)
Choice: plugin_configuration(plugin="auth") and configure(route="products/list", ...) (GP, 2026-11-15)

Consequences

  • The hook depends on applications_broadcast and @broadcast_hook of kajenn-org/kajenn#142, merged in develop with PR 147.
  • No application can have a route named plugin_configuration: issue 142 refuses a route with the name of a @broadcast_hook.
  • Carrying a change of the configuration to a spawned process is a general mechanism and is not part of this proposal. It does not exist today: until it does, a change made on a running server reaches only the applications of the main process. The live configuration is the subject of kajenn-org/kajenn#75; the requirement is noted there in a comment of 2026-11-15.
  • A recipe can open a route its author closed. The author who must prevent it redefines the hook.
  • The OpenAPI document follows the recipe with no other change: security is derived from the rule in force.
  • The configuration guide gets a section on plugin_configuration with the Shop example.
